inputs.text: [happily] Here comes the Triassic. [serious] About two hundred fifty million years ago. [playful] "Triassic" means "three": scientists found three layers of rock from this time, stacked up like a cake.
[excited] The very first ones! [calm] Small, running on two legs, super fast. [softly] Back then, nobody could guess they'd one day rule the whole Earth.
[curious] And what were the continents like?
[amazed] [pauses] Just one. One huge piece, all stuck together: Pangea. [calm] You could walk from America all the way to Africa without ever seeing the ocean.
[chuckles] Without a boat. [serious] It's hot everywhere, [softly] and really dry in the middle, far from the coast.
[happily] Conifers, [calm] like prickly pine trees, [softly] and cycads, [playful] which look like palm trees with spikes. [serious] But not one single flower yet.
[warmly] Plateosaurus munched on those plants all day long. [calm] A long neck, [softly] a small head, [excited] and about twenty-five feet long!

[serious] On land, almost nothing worried it. [pauses] But in the sea, [calm] a giant swam: Shonisaurus. [amazed] A sea reptile as long as a building lying on its side. [softly] It hunted fish and squid in deep water.
[curious] Is that one a dinosaur too?
[chuckles] No! [calm] Shonisaurus swam in the sea. [softly] Dinosaurs stayed on dry land.
[hesitant] Hey, [pauses] were there dinosaurs with horns yet?
[gently] Not yet. [softly] Triceratops doesn't exist yet. [calm] We'll have to wait a very, very long time.
[excited] After this, [pauses] the Earth gets even warmer, [softly] rain finally falls on the deserts, [happily] and the dinosaurs start to grow…
